MapITThe cheapest basket, in your zone.

Any list app can hold your shopping. None we know of prices it. MapIT takes the list you already write, prices the whole basket at every store inside a zone you draw, and answers the question that matters: where does this list cost least, once the driving is counted too.

WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

Everyone writes lists.
Nobody prices them.

A German consumer check found identical everyday products varying by more than 100% between stores in the same market, some staples by up to 400%. The savings sit in plain sight. The tools stop one step short of collecting them.

F·01

Leaflets are ads

The big grocery apps are digital brochures, promotions arranged by whoever paid for the page. They show you offers one at a time and leave the question untouched: what does my whole list cost at each store near me? You do that arithmetic in your head, in the aisle.

F·02

Pack prices lie

EU law forces shelves to show €/kg for a reason: the pack price alone misleads. It is getting worse: Germany's consumer centres track hidden price rises via shrinking packs averaging around 28% per product, and French law now forces stores to label shrinkflated goods. A basket comparison has to normalise to unit prices to compare anything.

F·03

The split-shop trap

Retail economics calls shoppers who split their basket across stores cherry-pickers, and the studies show they save more. The same maths that makes a split worth it can flip it into a loss: extra kilometres, extra time, extra fuel. No app we know of computes where that line sits. That is the FuelIT detour equation, pointed at a trolley.

F·04

Discounts priced in data

Loyalty apps trade discounts for purchase profiles; Germany's consumer federation litigated over how one major discounter app disclosed that "paying with data". A shopping list is an intimate document: it says who lives with you, what you can afford, what changed this month. It should never be the price of the discount.

IDENTICAL STAPLES VARIED UP TO 400% BETWEEN STORES IN ONE GERMAN CONSUMER CHECK
WHO IT SERVES

Built for everyone
who eats.

Our own trolleys first

The VF network runs real households and real properties, and the German side of the network shops in the most competitive grocery market in Europe, where discounters and full-range chains fight over every cent. MapIT proves itself the VF way: on our own supply runs, against our own receipts, before any customer touches it. If it can't beat what we already spend on the same list, it doesn't ship.

NOIRDA GMBH · DEVF EMPIRE CORP · MTRECEIPT-PROVEN

Households in the squeeze

German food prices rose over 13% in 2022 and another 12% in 2023, the fastest climb in a generation. For a family, the weekly basket is the one bill you can fight, and no app gives you a weapon for it.

Bulk buyers & big households

The bigger the basket, the bigger the absolute spread, and the more the brand-versus-own-brand question matters: brand products average around 50% over comparable own-brands in consumer testing. MapIT makes substitution a setting you choose once.

Small food businesses

Cafés, guesthouses and kitchens that buy retail because wholesale minimums don't fit. Their list barely changes week to week, which makes it the perfect thing to solve once and let the engine re-run each time prices move.

Shared households

One list, many hands. The whole house adds to it through the week; whoever ends up driving gets the solved run: which store, what to grab where, in what order. The house saves money without holding a meeting about it.

WHAT IT CHANGES

From a list on the fridge
to a solved run.

The measure of a shopping app is whether the run it sends you on was the cheapest way to buy those items in your zone. We judge MapIT on the receipt.

The whole basket.

Whole-list totals per store and per split combination, everything normalised to unit prices so shrinking packs and jumbo offers can't hide. One number per option: what this list costs you there.

Travel is a price.

A second store that saves €4 and burns €5 of fuel is not a saving. MapIT prices every extra kilometre with the same engine FuelIT uses for detours, and answers "stay in one store" when the split doesn't pay.

Your list stays yours.

A household's shopping is no one's raw material. MapIT processes lists to answer your question; they are never profiled, never traded for discounts, never sold. The architecture enforces this; there is no settings toggle.

THE MECHANICS

Four layers,
one run.

Built the VF way: deterministic mathematics doing the ranking, honest data underneath (every price carries its source and freshness), and a clean handoff at the end. MapIT decides the run, your navigator drives it. Like every VF system, it leaves the lab with the engine fitted and the harness tuned.

LAYER 1

The price lattice

Groceries have no official five-minute feed the way fuel does, so MapIT fuses what exists: retailer promotions and leaflet data, online-shop prices, and receipt-verified corrections from real purchases. Every price in the lattice carries a freshness stamp and a confidence score, and the maths respects both.

LAYER 2

The list twin

The engine reads your scribbled list as products: sizes, unit prices, and substitution rules you control, brand-only where it matters to you, open to own-brands where it doesn't. "Milk" becomes a decision the engine can price.

LAYER 3

Zone mathematics

You draw the zone, around home or along a route you're driving anyway. The engine scores every store inside it on the whole basket, then scores every sensible split across two or three stores again with the driving priced in litres and minutes. Sometimes the answer is one store, and the engine says so.

LAYER 4

The run

The output is a plan: which store first, what to buy where, in what order, and the route handed off to the navigator you already use. Shared lists mean the whole house fills it and one person runs it.

QUESTIONS

Asked.
Answered.

How does MapIT price my shopping list?

You write the list once. MapIT reads it as products with sizes, unit prices and substitution rules you control, then prices the whole basket at every store inside a zone you draw. Everything is normalised to unit prices, so shrinking packs and jumbo offers cannot hide. You get one number per option: what this list costs you there.

Does MapIT count the cost of driving to a second store?

Yes. A second store that saves €4 and burns €5 of fuel is no saving. MapIT scores every sensible split across two or three stores with the driving priced in litres and minutes, using the same engine FuelIT uses for detours. When the split does not pay, it answers with one store and says so.

Where do the grocery prices come from?

Groceries have no official five-minute feed the way fuel does, so MapIT fuses what exists: retailer promotions and leaflet data, online-shop prices, and receipt-verified corrections from real purchases. Every price in the lattice carries a freshness stamp and a confidence score, and the maths respects both. Coverage starts with your town's major grocers and expands.

Will MapIT sell my shopping data or show me ads?

No. MapIT processes lists to answer your question; they are never profiled, never traded for discounts and never sold. The architecture enforces this and there is no settings toggle. Your baskets stay on your device unless you pin them. MapIT sells neither ads nor you: the optional Plus tier is the only revenue.

What does MapIT cost?

The Core tier is free forever: basket compare across your town, with no ads and no data sales. Plus is €14.99 a year (€1.25 a month) and adds unlimited saved baskets, price history and automated trips. The price you join at is the price you renew at. These are planned launch figures; VF confirms them at each release.

Where does MapIT launch first?

Germany, Europe's most competitive grocery market, where the VF network's own supply runs are measured against real receipts week after week (R·01). R·02 is the public app: draw your zone, share the household list, set substitution rules and get the run, with price-drop alerts. R·03 fuses MapIT with FuelIT so one engine solves basket and tank on the same trip.
